rows.value: The book's entry 'Energy of Formation; Enthalpy of Formation' says the data are tabulated at 25 C and 1 bar with release of energy counted negative, that Table 28 lists selected components, and that the Fraunhofer ICT tabulated energies and enthalpies of formation 'including source references' in 1972, later the ICT Database of Thermochemical Values (more than 14 000 substances). Its reference list gives Medard, Tables Thermochimiques, Memorial de l'Artillerie Francaise, 415-492 (1954) as 'Vol. 23' in that entry and as '28' in its section 9, with the remark 'valid at 18 C and for carbon as diamond'

rows.lineage_root: the book itself; Muravyev 2021's ref 149 is the 2004 edition of the ICT Database (Kempa et al.)
rows.note: So the 2016 date is the compilation's, not the values': they trace to Medard 1954 and the ICT database, and agree with NIST where NIST also traces to Medard. The book's own statements conflict (25 C against 18 C, graphite against diamond: up to 1.9 kJ/mol per carbon atom). Muravyev's ref 166, Lobanov and Karmanova 1971, is the source of the two experimental nitroguanidine values -93.7 +/- 1.7 and -100 +/- 2.5 in his Table 1 (G44), so that paper is the one to fetch for nitroguanidine

rows.value: 214 compound entries with a property block were parsed from the alphabetical entries: 148 print an enthalpy of formation (151 lines in all), 145 an energy of formation, 169 a density, 114 a melting point, 96 an impact sensitivity, 55 a friction sensitivity, 65 a detonation velocity. Entries for mixtures and compositions have no molar mass and were not parsed. Footnotes say 'Computed by the ICT-Thermodynamic-Code' 7 times and 'quoted from' (Dobratz) 8 times, and 9 values are tagged '(calculated)' and 4 '(experimental)': all on heats of explosion or detonation; the formation-enthalpy lines carry no label
